citation: Shembrey C, et al. Principles of CRISPR-Cas13 mismatch intolerance enable selective silencing of point-mutated oncogenic RNA with single-base precision
what_it_anchors: CRISPR (RfxCas13d): mismatch NUMBER gates activity in a 23-nt spacer - 3 mismatches with the WT K-RAS transcript exceed the silencing limit, 2 with the SNP still silence it
claim: The two engineered crRNAs silence G12D by 54.8 and 39.9 percent and leave 11.0 and 17.9 percent WT silencing; the authors write that the differential is 'likely attributable to three mismatches with WT KRAS - exceeding the upper limit of mismatches that allow for efficient silencing - but only two mismatches with the G12D and G12C variants', and that over half of crRNAs with 2 mismatches with the SNV show SNV-selective silencing. Central-region mismatches are the most intolerant; the paper states Cas13d has no seed region
claim_kind: magnitude with a threshold (in-cell silencing percent), NOT a diagnostic fluorescence fold-change
access_detail: Europe PMC fullTextXML; numbers are prose and figures only (no table-wrap element in the XML), so nothing is taken from a supplement

citation: Chen Y, et al. Universal and high-fidelity DNA single nucleotide polymorphism detection based on a CRISPR/Cas12a biochip
what_it_anchors: CRISPR (Cas12a): one designed extra mismatch next to the SNP site multiplies the allele signal ratio from about 2-fold to about 10-fold
claim: The fully complementary guide 'produced a fluorescent signal only twice as strong as that produced by a single nucleotide mismatch, and the signal strength again decreased by nearly ten times when we added the additional nucleotide u mismatch adjacent to the mutant site'; the figure states 'An additional nucleotide mismatch improves the SNR from 2-fold to nearly 10-fold'
claim_kind: magnitude (fold signal at a fixed guide-target pair), figure-level
access_detail: Europe PMC fullTextXML; read from the Results prose and the Fig. 3 caption

citation: Molina Vargas AM, et al. New design strategies for ultra-specific CRISPR-Cas13a-based RNA detection with single-nucleotide mismatch sensitivity
what_it_anchors: CRISPR (LbuCas13a): whether a single mismatch matters at all depends on SPACER LENGTH and target concentration, not on position alone
claim: With a 20-nt spacer, mismatches at +7, +8, +9 give 'up to a 70 percent reduction in activity, compared to a perfect-match' system, and a position-7 mismatch costs about 40 percent of signal-to-noise while positions 4 and 11 stay within 20 percent; a 28-nt spacer shows 'no single mismatch discriminatory capacity at the target-RNA concentrations tested'; a 16-nt spacer 'still required a perfect match for RNase activity'
claim_kind: magnitude with a boundary condition (spacer length x concentration), figure-level
access_detail: Europe PMC fullTextXML; read from the Results prose

citation: Larsen BB, et al. RNA structure modulates Cas13 activity and enables mismatch detection
what_it_anchors: CRISPR (Cas13): without an occluder most single mismatches are inert or insignificant, so a per-mismatch fold-signal is not transferable
claim: Without a crRNA occluder only 74/96 mismatches (77 percent) lowered activity at all and discrimination was significant in only 13/24 (54 percent); with the occluder 24/24 were significant and specificity improved about 50-fold, measured as the maximum ratio of WT to mismatch fluorescence. The authors state the ability to distinguish was 'not guaranteed for any crRNA for any of the mismatch positions we tested'
claim_kind: negative result plus a ratio improvement, not an absolute magnitude
access_detail: Europe PMC fullTextXML; read from the Results prose; NIH author manuscript (NIHMS2119695)

citation: Wu X, et al. Thermodynamically programmed one-pot CRISPR platform for point-of-care SNP genotyping
what_it_anchors: CRISPR (Cas12a, one-pot): SNP vs WT allele contrast in fluorescence is a tunable quantity, 2.8-18.4-fold, set by the PAM triplet
claim: Systematic PAM substitution 'yielded tunable genotype separation: canonical PAMs (TTT) produced 2.8-6.0-fold discrimination between SNP and WT alleles, whereas suboptimal PAM variants (ATT) further elevated contrast to 5.9-18.4-fold'. The paper also states 'predictive design rules for SNP discrimination remain incomplete, necessitating empirical validation for new targets'
claim_kind: magnitude (fold allele contrast) with an explicit no-predictive-rule caveat
access_detail: Europe PMC fullTextXML; read from the Results prose; figure ranges

citation: Imai K, Ohama Y, Sato K, et al. Loop-mediated isothermal amplification assays for the rapid discrimination of Treponema pallidum strains
what_it_anchors: LAMP: an allele call can be carried by the melting peak, not by the amplification time - SS14 92.46 C vs Nichols 93.71 C
claim: Melting curve analysis 'produced a single peak at 92.46 C +/- 0.13 C and 93.71 C +/- 0.21 C for SS14-LAMP and Nichols-LAMP, respectively', with a stated +/- 1 C margin for variant assignment; a QProbe mismatched to the amplicon 'melt[s] at a lower Tm'. No cross-reaction up to 2.0e4 plasmid copies
claim_kind: magnitude (endpoint melting separation 1.25 C); the primer-site mismatch itself is not quantified
access_detail: Europe PMC fullTextXML; read from the Results prose
